text: Everyone here gets a warning label. What is yours, and who ignores theirs?
why: cheap, funny, and quietly a roast

text: This group is a country. What is the flag, and what is banned first?
why: absurd state-building, everyone can answer

text: Name this group's official anthem, then perform the first line like you mean it.
why: category error, immediate embarrassment

text: Describe this group as a reality show, then say who gets the villain edit.
why: the answer is always a person in the room

text: Rank the room by who steals food, then by who lies about it.
why: harmless until it isn't

text: Pick one: betray them first or last.
why: six words, whole table picks a side

text: Name the group's weakest link.
why: five words, maximum damage

text: Would you rather have this group see your search history or your camera roll?
why: pick your poison, no way to look good

text: Pick who here dies first in a horror film.
why: they all already know the answer

text: Rank the room by who lies most.
why: everyone starts defending themselves

text: What would you delete first?
why: five words, everyone pictures their own phone

text: What is your worst trait?
why: deceptively hard, answers are revealing

text: A film is made about this group's worst night. What is the title, and who plays you?
why: forces the group to agree on the worst night

text: The group wakes up in a cult you founded. What is the rule everyone follows, and who leaves first?
why: invents a world and casts the deserter

text: You get one hour alone with everyone's phones. What do you do, and who never forgives you?
why: temptation plus consequence, no props needed

text: A genie gives this group one wish that you will all regret. What is it?
why: the regret is the punchline

text: You find a card that buys whatever you say out loud. What does this group do first, and what breaks first?
why: chaos with a built-in crash

text: You all get 24 hours to become famous. Who succeeds, who commits a felony, who holds the camera?
why: assigns three roles, nobody escapes

text: One of you is a spy planted by the group chat. Who is the most convincing, and who cracks first?
why: paranoia with a group answer

text: Give everyone here a criminal alias and the crime they are known for, starting with yourself.
why: crime as story, and you go first

text: Invent a religion for this group. Name the god, the holy day, and the first heretic.
why: absurd, but it will get uncomfortably accurate

text: Pitch the worst possible business this group could start together, and name the first employee to quit.
why: the pitch always describes the group

text: Write this group's three laws. Then admit which one you break most.
why: legislation followed by a confession

text: Invent the rumour that would tear this group apart fastest, and say who starts it.
why: the room starts planning before the answer

text: Give every person here a role in a heist, including the one who gets caught.
why: casting the fall guy to his face

text: Rank the room by who would sell the others out first, and for what.
why: rank plus price, so it is a betrayal, not a list

text: Rank the room by who would survive a cult, then by who would run it.
why: two orders, two insults

text: Would you rather know every secret in this room or have every secret here known by the person to your left?
why: no answer is safe

text: Would you rather be the one who betrays the group or the one who never finds out?
why: cowardice versus ignorance, both lose

text: Would you rather be remembered as a liar or as a coward?
why: eleven words, instant argument

text: Pick the person here most likely to become a cult leader, and name the cult.
why: the second half is where it gets funny

text: Pick the person here who would eat a stranger's leftovers without asking.
why: specific, gross, instantly decided

text: Give the room your worst theory about why someone here is the way they are.
why: an accusation dressed as a theory

text: Describe the version of this group that would exist if you had never joined.
why: self-erasure, and the room has to answer honestly

text: Say what you think the person opposite would say about you if you left the room.
why: they can confirm or deny, which is worse

text: Describe this group's worst night as if you were reporting it on the news.
why: the format forces the detail out

text: Tell the group the first thing you would change about them if you could.
why: collective insult, no individual to blame

text: Rate your own loyalty out of ten, then say what would move it.
why: the second clause is the confession

text: The group gets one hour to hide a body. What is your job, and who panics first?
why: absurd crime plus a coward

text: You wake up as this group's dictator. What is your first decree, and who is executed for it?
why: the execution answer is always personal

text: The group is trapped in this room with a zombie outside. What is the plan, and who is bitten first?
why: survival plus a sacrifice, in one turn

text: You can erase one person here from history, but everyone remembers them. Who, and what is the cover story?
why: the cover story is the tell

text: You are all in a Saw trap. Who solves it, who sacrifices themselves, who is the traitor?
why: three roles, and the traitor is a real accusation

text: The group is on a sinking boat with one seat. Who takes it, and who pretends to be fine?
why: the pretender is the interesting answer

text: If this group had to eat one person here to survive, who cooks, who refuses, who asks for seconds?
why: the seconds answer is the whole game

text: This group has to pick one member to take the blame for a crime nobody committed. Who goes?
why: a vote with a real cost

text: What is the worst thing you have done to someone in this room and never admitted?
why: the shelf's thesis question

text: What is the biggest lie you are still keeping alive in front of this group?
why: present tense, so it is a live risk

text: Who here have you secretly written off, and what did they do?
why: the second clause stops it being a shrug

text: What would you say at the funeral of the person to your right that you would never say now?
why: the honest eulogy nobody delivers

text: Which person here would you leave behind in an emergency, and what is your excuse?
why: the excuse is the confession

text: What have you stolen from someone in this room?
why: nine words, immediate silence

text: Which secret of yours would end a friendship here if it came out?
why: everyone starts guessing which one

text: What do you actually think of the person to your left, in one sentence?
why: no cushioning allowed, to their face

text: What is the meanest thing you have said about someone here behind their back?
why: the room already knows the answer

text: Who here would you refuse to help at 3 AM, and what would you tell them?
why: the excuse has to be said out loud

text: What is the thing you have done that would change how this room sees you?
why: open enough to be honest, specific enough to be real

text: What is the worst thing you have done while someone here covered for you?
why: implicates two people at once

text: Whose trust here are you actively betraying right now?
why: present tense again, and everyone checks themselves

text: What is the thing you would never confess to this group, and why not?
why: the reason is more revealing than the thing

text: What is the last lie you told the person to your left?
why: one specific person, one specific lie

text: Who here knows the worst version of you, and what did they see?
why: a compliment and a threat

text: What is the most damage you have done to a friendship without being caught?
why: the uncaught part is the point

text: What is the worst advice you have given a friend on purpose?
why: on purpose changes everything

text: What do you owe someone here that you never intend to repay?
why: a debt and a refusal in one sentence

text: Who here talks the biggest game and delivers the least, and what was the last promise?
why: the promise is the receipt

text: Who here is one bad week away from ruining their life, and what tips it?
why: the room goes quiet, then someone laughs

text: Who here would sell out this group for a free holiday, and where would they go?
why: the destination makes it funny instead of cruel

text: Who here is the reason a night got out of hand, and what did they do?
why: collectively agreed before anyone answers

text: Ring the last person you argued with and let the room listen to the first ten seconds.
why: real person, real time, no script

text: Text the person you lied to most recently and ask them if they know.
why: one message, irreversible

text: Call the person who would be least surprised to hear from you at this hour and say why.
why: the word least is the whole dare

text: Read out the message you sent about someone here that you would not want forwarded.
why: the room is about to learn who talks

text: Show the room what is in your recently deleted, and say why it went.
why: deleted means it mattered

text: Say the worst thing you have done to someone here, and do not soften the delivery.
why: the delivery is graded by the room

text: Tell the room the last time you were relieved someone here failed.
why: nobody admits this sober and honest

text: Name who here you would trust with your life and who you would not. Both, to their faces.
why: the second half is compulsory

text: Admit what you would do with one hour alone in this room with everyone's phones.
why: admitting the plan is worse than the plan

text: Tell the room the biggest lie you are currently telling someone in this group.
why: live ammunition

text: Name the person here who has most disappointed you, and say why to their face.
why: eye contact required by the sentence

text: Pick a person here and describe the worst thing you think they have done.
why: a guess that lands like an accusation

text: Admit the lowest thing you have done for a laugh.
why: comedy with a cost

text: Tell the room what you would trade to undo your worst decision this year.
why: the trade is the confession

text: Say what you would erase from your history with someone here.
why: everyone has one, nobody names it easily

text: Name the person here you would abandon first in a crisis, while looking at them.
why: the physical instruction makes it stick

text: Tell the room the last secret you kept from them.
why: specific, recent, checkable

text: Explain, without naming them, which person here you are least honest with.
why: the room solves it in four seconds

text: Read out the meanest thing you have ever written about someone in this room.
why: written evidence, read aloud

text: Confess the small revenge nobody here ever traced back to you.
why: never found out means it is still live

text: Name the person here who would cover for you and the person who would tell everyone. Both.
why: two names, one of them is an insult

text: Describe this group's worst night as a news report, without laughing.
why: the format drags the details out

text: Say what you would tell your younger self about this group, in one sentence.
why: a warning someone here needs to hear

text: Call a friend and ask them what they think of this group. Play it on speaker.
why: an outside verdict on the room

text: Tell the room the worst thing you know about the person to your right.
why: specific target, no escape

text: Admit the last time you lied to get out of seeing someone here.
why: everyone here has done it

text: Name the person here whose life you would not swap, then say why.
why: a compliment that still has to be justified

text: Name the person here you would want with you in a fight and the one you would leave.
why: two names, both said out loud

text: Tell the room the last thing you would want read out at your funeral.
why: dark, funny, and about them

text: Admit what you have broken and blamed someone here for.
why: this one gets a name

text: Say the worst thing you have thought about someone in this room this week.
why: this week keeps it honest

text: Name what you would need to hear from someone here to forgive them.
why: quiet, and the room hears who it is

text: Read out the last note you wrote to yourself.
why: unfiltered, and nobody expects the answer

text: Describe the most illegal thing you have witnessed, without naming anyone.
why: story, not instruction

text: Name the last person you blocked, and what they did.
why: small, recent, specific

text: Tell the room what you would do if you knew you would never be caught.
why: the no-guardrails card

text: Describe your worst intrusive thought from this week, out loud.
why: the room will not forget the answer

text: Admit the last time you were glad someone here got hurt.
why: the worst admission on the shelf

text: Name the person here you have lied to most, and look at them.
why: nine words plus eye contact

text: Redo the answer while staring at the person you named.
why: turns a name into a confrontation

text: Give the answer again, standing, like a confession.
why: physical form changes the delivery

text: Say the same answer but replace every name with a job title.
why: funny, and it dodges nothing

text: Answer again in the voice of the person you betrayed.
why: imitation as an admission

text: Repeat the answer, but whisper the last sentence.
why: the whisper lands harder

text: Give the answer again with one hand on the shoulder of whoever you just named.
why: contact makes the room lean in
